For alarm status, the GUI shall also issue an audible alarm, and the icon shall be different from the okay status for that device. The visual alarm shall include a change of color for the affected device.
3.2.1.4.7. There shall be an option to turn off the audible alarm permanently or temporarily for a given period.
3.2.1.4.8. The alarm icon shall change to the normal status icon automatically when the alarm condition is removed. Alarm conditions shall be configurable on the screen.
3.2.1.4.9. When a device status has been overridden,

1 The RLCS shall monitor all field device sensors, and shall process operator requests for changing field device status.
3.2.2.2 Any operator or system command, which changes the state of field control devices, must be checked for integrity at multiple levels in the RLCS.
3.2.2.3 The RLCS software shall monitor, display, and update the database with the status of all system field elements. Any change in device state shall be reported on the screen not later than 2 seconds from the time it occurs. In addition to monitoring field devices the system shall also monitor field controllers and connected on the RLCS network for control system integrity. The system shall report any users logged in RLCS network computers any time and all commands issued in the field units.
3.2.2.

4 During ‘degraded’ mode, the system shall monitor device sensors at the frequency rate stored in the database to take effect only during ‘degraded’ mode. In general, the system shall monitor the status of all field devices at the frequency specified in the System Control Parameters for that mode.
3.2.2.4.1 The system shall control all system field elements to device sensor level for those device sensors that may be controlled. For example, the temperature sensor at the controller cabinet is not a controllable sensor, whereas the ‘gate arm control lines’ sensor may be controlled.
3.2.2.4.2 Each device control command shall check the current status of all closure devices in the system and shall abort if any closure control device status is unknown.

3.2.2.4.4 The current status for all devices shall be maintained at each controller unit.
3.2.2.4.5 Alarms
Check Device Status for Alarm Condition
Each status received from device sensors shall be checked against alarm conditions for that device sensor and the status will be updated to indicate an alarm.
3.2.2.4.6 Critical alarms shall be generated when one or more of these conditions are met.
1) A closure device changes from a known state to unknown state (status lost)
2) A closure device changes from legal state to illegal state. E.g. pop-ups in the down position when they are supposed to be up.
3) The control system Integrity verification indicates a verification failure.

5 Field devices shall receive respond to commands from the RLCS within 12 seconds of the command confirmation being issued by the operator using a keyboard (or other input device).
3.3.2 User Interface (GUI)
Priority: Must have
3.3.2.1 The RLCS shall support multiple users logged on, up to the limit of the number of users defined in the database.
3.3.2.2 Not including device and network response times, requests from the GUI for status updates shall not exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display.
Not including device and network response time, requests from the GUI for device status changes (control commands) shall not exceed 2 seconds.
3.3.2.3 The facility map on the screen shall refresh every 2 seconds but can be configurable within the database to more than 2 seconds by the user.

This diagram illustrates a system architecture for monitoring and controlling RLCS Field Devices, composed of internal functions (round shapes), external entities or functions (square shapes), data flows (solid lines), and control flows (dashed lines).

The central function is “Monitor Devices 3.2.2.1”, which receives “Device Sensor Status” from multiple sources: directly from “RLCS Field Devices” (external entity), from “Set Alarms 3.2.2.3”, and from “Collect Log Data 3.2.2.7”. It also sends “Device Sensor Status” to “Track # of Failed Device Commands 3.2.2.5” and to “Process GUI Commands 3.2.2.4”. Additionally, it outputs “Command Failure Data” to “Track # of Failed Device Commands 3.2.2.5”.

“Track # of Failed Device Commands 3.2.2.

5” receives “Command Failure Count” from “Monitor Devices 3.2.2.1” and sends “Command Data (for retry)” to “Control Devices 3.2.2.2”.

“Control Devices 3.2.2.2” sends “Device Sensor Command” via a dashed control flow line to “RLCS Field Devices”. It also receives “Command Data” from “GUI 3.2.1” and from “Process GUI Commands 3.2.2.4”.

“GUI 3.2.1” (external entity) sends “Command Data” to both “Process GUI Commands 3.2.2.4” and “Control Devices 3.2.2.2”.

“Process GUI Commands 3.2.2.4” receives “Command Data” from “GUI 3.2.1” and “Device Sensor Initialization Data” from “Identify & Initialize all Devices 3.2.2.6”. It also receives “Command”, “Device Description”, “Device Sensor Status”, and “Security Level” from “Data Processing and Security 3.2.4”. It sends “Command Data” back to “GUI 3.

2.1” and to “Control Devices 3.2.2.2”.

“Identify & Initialize all Devices 3.2.2.6” receives “Device Sensor Initialization Data” from “Data Processing and Security 3.2.4” and sends the same data to “Process GUI Commands 3.2.2.4”.

“Set Alarms 3.2.2.3” receives “Device Sensor Alarm Criteria” and “Device Sensor Status” from “Data Processing and Security 3.2.4”, and sends “Device Status” to “Monitor Devices 3.2.2.1”.

“Collect Log Data 3.2.2.7” receives “Device Sensor Status” from “Monitor Devices 3.2.2.1” and sends “Device Sensor Status” to “Data Processing and Security 3.2.4”.

The diagram below shows the flow of information to and from the different interfaces.
This diagram illustrates the architecture and data flow of a Reversible Lane Control System (RLCS) integrated with other traffic management systems. The central component is the RLCS, which communicates bidirectionally via solid lines (existing connections) with several key elements:

- **Reversible Lane Changeable Message Signs**: Receives “Message Number Control Commands” and sends back “Device Status”.
- **Reversible Lane Field Devices** (gates, pop-up, lights): Receives “Device Control Commands” and sends back “Device Status”.
- **RLCS Operator**: Exchanges “RLCS Status and Control” information.
